subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: DNA is described as a polymer with what overall shape?
questions.explain: DNA is a double helix, two strands twisted together, made of repeating nucleotide units (a polymer).

questions.q: What is the main difference between a stem cell and a specialised cell such as a nerve cell?
options: A stem cell has more chromosomes
A stem cell is unspecialised and can divide to form different cell types
A specialised cell can become any other type of cell
questions.explain: Stem cells are unspecialised and can differentiate into many cell types, unlike specialised cells.

questions.q: Which of these shows genetic variation rather than environmental variation?
options: A footballer's strong leg muscles from training
A person being tanned after sunbathing
A plant grown in shade being taller and thinner
questions.explain: Blood group is determined entirely by genes (genetic variation); the others are influenced by the environment.

questions.q: How many cells are produced from one parent cell by mitosis?
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical cells (meiosis, not mitosis, makes four).

questions.q: What is a stem cell?
options: A cell that can no longer divide
An undifferentiated cell that can divide to form different types of cell
A cell that has lost its nucleus
questions.explain: Stem cells are undifferentiated cells able to divide and differentiate into specialised cells.

questions.q: What happens to the DNA during the cell cycle before a cell divides by mitosis?
options: The chromosomes pair up and swap genes
The DNA is replicated so each chromosome forms two identical copies
questions.explain: Before mitosis the DNA replicates so each chromosome consists of two identical strands.

questions.q: During which stage of the cell cycle do the chromosomes line up in the middle and separate to opposite ends of the cell?
questions.explain: In mitosis the duplicated chromosomes line up and are pulled to opposite poles before the cell divides.

questions.q: Different versions of the same gene are called:
questions.explain: Alleles are different forms of a gene, for example for eye colour.

questions.q: A recessive allele is only expressed in the phenotype when:
options: It is paired with a dominant allele
questions.explain: A recessive allele is only shown when both alleles are recessive, as a dominant allele would mask it.

questions.q: What is the genome of an organism?
options: The entire genetic material of that organism
questions.explain: The genome is the entire genetic material (all the DNA) of an organism.

questions.q: What are chromosomes made of?
questions.explain: Chromosomes are made of long DNA molecules that carry genes.

questions.q: What is the difference between genotype and phenotype?
options: They mean exactly the same thing
Genotype is the physical appearance; phenotype is the alleles
Genotype is the alleles present; phenotype is the physical characteristics
questions.explain: Genotype is the combination of alleles, while phenotype is the observable characteristic produced.

questions.q: What is differentiation?
options: A cell dividing into two identical cells
A cell becoming specialised for a particular function
questions.explain: Differentiation is the process by which cells become specialised for a specific job.

questions.q: Polydactyly (extra fingers/toes) is caused by a dominant allele. This means it:
options: Can be inherited from just one affected parent
Only appears when both alleles are present
questions.explain: As polydactyly is dominant, only one copy of the allele is needed, so one affected parent can pass it on.

questions.q: Which structure carries the genetic information and is made of DNA?
questions.explain: Chromosomes are made of long DNA molecules that carry many genes coding for proteins.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: Meiosis produces:
questions.explain: Meiosis produces four non-identical haploid gametes, each with half the normal number of chromosomes.

questions.q: A typical human body cell contains how many chromosomes?
questions.explain: Human body cells are diploid with 46 chromosomes (23 pairs).

questions.q: During which part of the cell cycle does the cell grow and copy its DNA and sub-cellular structures, before mitosis begins?
questions.explain: Before mitosis, in interphase, the cell grows, increases its number of organelles and copies its DNA.

questions.q: The two cells produced by mitosis are:
questions.explain: Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.

questions.q: Gametes (sex cells) such as sperm and egg are described as haploid because they contain:
options: Twice the normal number of chromosomes
Half the normal number of chromosomes (23 in humans)
questions.explain: Gametes are haploid, carrying a single set of chromosomes (23 in humans) so the full number is restored at fertilisation.

questions.q: Identical twins have the same genes but can still show small differences. These differences are caused by:
questions.explain: Identical twins share the same genotype, so any differences between them are due to environmental factors.
